words.explanation: n. [U] a feeling of sadness because sth. is not as good as you expected or has not happened in the way you hoped 失望；沮丧
words.example: We could see the disappointment in her eyes.

words.explanation: n. [C] a person who reports news from a particular country or on a particular subject for a newspaper or a television or radio station 记者；通讯员
words.example: I was a correspondent for The New York Times before I came to China.

words.explanation: n. [C] sth. that delays or prevents progress, or makes things worse than they were 阻碍前进的事物；挫折
words.example: She has suﬀered a serious setback in her political career.

words.explanation: n. [C, usu. sing.] a return to being powerful, popular, or famous again after being unpopular or unknown for a long time 东山再起；再度流行
words.example: The miniskirt made a comeback in the late 1980s.

words.explanation: vi. to turn quickly on your feet so that you face in the opposite direction（以脚为支点）转身
words.example: She pivots gracefully on the stage.

words.explanation: n. [C] sb. who knows a lot about a particular subject, esp. one that is not a science subject 学者（尤指精通某一门文科学问的人）
n. [C, U] very bad luck, or sth. that happens to you as a result of bad luck 不幸；厄运；不幸事故；灾难
words.example: I had the misfortune to share a room with someone who snored loudly.

words.explanation: ad. for all future time; always 永远
words.example: I think that we will live together forever.

words.explanation: a. needing electricity to work, produced by electricity, or used for carrying electricity 用电的；电动的；用来导电的
words.example: Is the car electric or gas?

words.explanation: n. [C] ( or light ~ ) 灯泡
n. [C] a record player 留声机；电唱机
n. [C] a movie 电影
n. [C, U] a scientific test done to find out how sth. will react in a particular situation, or to find out if a particular idea is true 实验
words.example: This experiment does no harm to the environment.

words.explanation: n. [C, U] the act of not accepting, believing in, or agreeing with sth. 拒绝；摈弃
words.example: Their rejection of the plan is a blow to us.

words.explanation: n. [C] a person or company whose business is to arrange the writing, production, and sale of books, newspapers, etc.（书、报纸等的） 出版者；出版商；出版社
n. [C] 主题公园
n. [C] sb. who introduces changes and new ideas 革新者；创新者
n. [C] sb. who has just started to do or learn sth. 生手；初学者
n. [C, U] a strong human feeling such as love, hate, or anger 强烈的情感；激情
words.example: Mom received the bad news without showing any visible sign of emotion.

words.explanation: ad. always or in every situation 总是；必定；必然
n. [C] sb. who is always hopeful and always believes that good things will happen 乐观者；乐观主义者
words.example: Every change is a change for the better to an optimist.

words.explanation: n. [U] slight pain or a bad feeling 不舒服；不适
words.example: A cushion will help reduce the discomfort of sitting on the ﬂoor.

words.explanation: n. [C, U] an annoying problem or situation, esp. one that forces you to make an extra effort to do sth. 不方便；不便之处；（尤指）麻烦事
words.example: We apologize for any inconvenience the delayed ﬂight has caused you.

words.explanation: a. happening after a very short time 突然间的
words.example: The play was an overnight success.

words.explanation: vt. to encourage sb. by making them feel confident and eager to achieve sth. great 鼓舞；激励
words.example: The country needs a leader who can inspire its people.

words.explanation: n. [C, U] a very strong deeply felt emotion 强烈的情感；激情
words.example: She spoke with great passion about her plan for the drama club.

words.explanation: ad. in a manner that is relating to feelings and the way they affect your life 感情上地
words.example: We are still emotionally attached to our parents after graduation.

words.explanation: if a letter, number, picture, or sign stands for sth., it represents a word, name, or idea, esp. in a short form 代表；象征；意味着
words.example: In many cultures, the gesture "V" stands for victory.

words.explanation: to have the same interests, attitudes, qualities, etc. as another person or group（与某人）在某方面有共同之处
words.example: He does not have much in common with the other kids in high school.

words.explanation: to go above or beyond the limits of sth. 超越；克服
words.example: He has managed to rise above the financial problems and finished the task on time.

words.explanation: to take the correct action for a problem, piece of work, etc. 处理
words.example: We must deal with the difficult situation before it gets out of control.

words.explanation: to adopt 采用；采纳；采取
words.example: He took on new ways of life after he got married.

words.explanation: used for talking about people or things that are better than all others that have existed 有史以来（最好）的
words.example: Who's your favorite basketball player of all time?

words.explanation: to get rid of sth. 摆脱；废除
words.example: Do you think we should do away with old traditions?

words.explanation: to make a mistake during a process so that you do not get the right result（在过程中）出错，弄错
words.example: Follow these instructions and you won't go wrong.

words.explanation: not always or not in every situation 不一定；未必
words.example: Our customers won't necessarily understand why we are raising our prices.
